clue.text: Bill serves traditional meal without a drink

indicators.note: without tells us to take the letter A away from the meal word

parts.note: a Sunday roast is the traditional British meal
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A waiter brings out a classic dinner but no drink with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' drops the A from ROAST to leave ROST; add RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a bird's beak, and a beak is also called a bill.

clue.text: Stood to cheer when given such wine

parts.note: stood up means rose
hip, as in 'hip hip hooray', is a cheer

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to cheer when handed a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when given' is a link; 'such wine' refers to the kind of home-made wine produced from the fruit of the wild rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Country wine is often brewed from the red fruit of the wild rose bush.

clue.text: A garment to make one perspire?

explanation.surface: A woolly top that leaves its wearer hot and damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper is a knitted garment; read literally, anything that makes you sweat could bear the name.

clue.text: What orientals may paint on and eat

definitions.text: What orientals may paint on and eat

parts.words: What orientals may paint on and eat
parts.note: a thin edible sheet from Asia, used both for painting and as a wrapper on food

explanation.surface: Asking what material in the Far East serves both artists and cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin edible sheet, made from plant pith or grain, is used in Asian art and in spring rolls and sweets.

clue.text: Incisive Missouri road-worker

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted labourer mending the highways in Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and cutting, which is what incisive means.

clue.text: No short distance for a fielder

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder positioned a long way from the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthy stage of a journey is the first sense; in cricket, the second names a deep fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.

clue.text: Radical artist involved in defamation case

indicators.note: involved in means one piece is set inside the letters of the other

parts.note: a libel is a defamation, and a libel case goes to court
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A firebrand painter is caught up in a defamation lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically, radical and progressive views are described as broad-minded and free-thinking.

clue.text: Row results when I come in to pry

indicators.note: come in to means the letter I goes inside the snooping word

parts.note: to nose about is to pry

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out when someone starts prying.
explanation.definitionFit: A row (rhyming with 'cow') is a loud din or racket.

clue.text: Freighter carrying less freight

explanation.surface: A cargo vessel sailing with a reduced load.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge used to unload ships is one sense; a vessel with less load weighs less, the comparative sense.

clue.text: He's a divine man, and utterly liberated

parts.note: a divine being is a god

indicators.note: utterly here means uttered, spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: liberated means free

explanation.surface: A holy man who is completely set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' is read as 'in utterance': FREE said out loud gives FREY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Sister hoards money to get a jacket

indicators.note: hoards means the abbreviation for sister keeps the money inside it

parts.note: pence is money

explanation.surface: A nun saves up her coins to buy a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short close-fitting jacket, named after an Earl.

clue.text: Game deputy-head made a spanner

parts.note: bridge is a card game
the head, or first letter, of deputy is D

explanation.surface: A deputy head teacher plays cards and fixes something with a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like a tool, but here it is something that spans, like a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a span across a gap, such as a river, is to build a crossing over it.

clue.text: Prior to setback man appears agitated

indicators.note: prior to puts the man before the next piece

parts.note: he is a man
set is put, and back turns it round, so set back gives TUP

explanation.surface: A man is clearly upset before some setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or flustered is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: High-flown communication

parts.note: high-flown usually means pretentious, but here a message literally flown in a plane

explanation.surface: Pompous, grandiloquent writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogramme is a lightweight letter sent by plane.

clue.text: Primate sheltered by section of earthwork

indicators.note: sheltered by means the primate is protected inside the section

parts.note: a part is a section
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey hides in a part of a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall or bank on a fortification is this defence.

clue.text: A fish to thrash its victims

parts.note: to lam is to beat, thrash
prey are victims

explanation.surface: A predatory fish that beats its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: This jawless eel-like creature is a fish that sucks blood from other fish.

clue.text: Grave offence committed by men at home

parts.note: mortals are men, human beings
in means at home

explanation.surface: A serious crime is committed by men in their own houses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching this is a grave, deadly sin.

clue.text: A port made in new Orleans

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of Orleans are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A harbour built in New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' looks like the city, but 'new' is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a southern Italian port city.

clue.text: Make society milliner go to pieces

parts.note: a hatter makes hats, as a milliner does

explanation.surface: Causing a fashionable hatmaker to break down.
explanation.definitionFit: To break into fragments is to go to pieces.

clue.text: Heather catches a couple of pages drinking

indicators.note: catches means the heather word holds the pages inside it

parts.note: ling is a type of heather
P is page, so two pages are PP

explanation.surface: Heather snagging two pages while someone drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat drinking milk with its tongue is doing this.

clue.text: Supervise old cleric's return to diocese

indicators.note: return means the cleric's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for reverend, is a cleric
a bishop's see is a diocese

explanation.surface: Asking an old priest to come back to the diocese to keep watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over or manage is to supervise.

clue.text: Socialist restricted by barrier displays ennui

indicators.note: restricted by means the socialist sits within the barrier

parts.note: a boom is a floating barrier across a harbour
red is a socialist

explanation.surface: A left-winger penned behind a barrier, looking weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is the French word for listless weariness.

clue.text: Wager I'm to get points for being early

parts.note: a wager is a bet
taken as written, without the apostrophe
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Betting on points to finish first.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning in good time, early in the day.

clue.text: Record-holding diver ordered to strip

indicators.note: holding means the reordered letters keep the record inside
ordered means the letters of diver are put in a new order

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record-breaking diver told to take off clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns DIVER into DRIVE; 'holding' puts EP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away from or deny someone something is to strip them of it.

clue.text: Cheat me out of a knife

indicators.note: out of here means the letters are made out of the earlier words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is swindled out of a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, broad-bladed chopping knife.

clue.text: Army extras must return here now

indicators.note: must return means the army letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, the part-time reserve soldiers
present means here

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers must report back here immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is Britain's Territorial Army of volunteer reservists.
explanation.definitionFit: At this time or currently means now.

clue.text: Final stanza read in gently-spoken voice

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Reading the last verse in a soft voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The short closing stanza of a ballade or poem.

clue.text: Jelly with a pungent flavour endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: spicy means having a pungent flavour

explanation.surface: A savoury jelly with a sharp taste that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock.

clue.text: Criminals targeting woman in the closer house

indicators.note: in means the woman is placed inside the words for the nearer house

parts.note: the house nearer to us is this house, not that one
Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: Burglars targeting a woman in a house close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the closer of two things, so 'the closer house' is this house.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbers and burglars are criminals.

clue.text: Huge crowd I have to follow

parts.note: a mass is a crowd
I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A big crowd that I must follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means enormous, very big.

clue.text: Play it in students' charity week!

definitions.text: Play it in students' charity week!

parts.words: Play it in students' charity week!
parts.note: students' charity week is rag week, and time is a playful word for week; also a music to play

explanation.surface: Encouraging music during student fundraising week.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a syncopated style of jazz piano music.

clue.text: Frank, from then on, attended bible lessons

parts.note: since means from then on
RE is religious education, school bible lessons

explanation.surface: Frank went to Sunday school ever since.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means honest and genuine.
